outboundPolicy.title: Outbound access policy
outboundPolicy.description: Ordinary private hosts are allowed by default. Enable strict mode to restrict management-node HTTP access to an explicit allowlist.
outboundPolicy.permanent: Cloud metadata, link-local and special reserved addresses are always blocked, even when strict mode is off or an allowlist entry matches.
outboundPolicy.adminOnly: Administrator permission is required to view or change the outbound policy.
outboundPolicy.restrictHelp: Off by default. When enabled, private destinations must match the allowlist. Turning this off preserves the list.
outboundPolicy.hostsHelp: One hostname, IP address or CIDR per line. No wildcard hostnames. This list is used only in strict mode.
outboundPolicy.persisted: Saving writes outbound_restrict_private_hosts and outbound_allow_private_hosts to server.yaml and applies them immediately.
outboundPolicy.readOnly: The server configuration is read-only or has no writable configuration file. An administrator must make server.yaml writable before saving.
outboundPolicy.failed: The outbound policy could not be loaded or saved. Retry without changing the draft.

updates.title: Version and updates
updates.description: Check and update the server, the system image catalog and the inference template catalog here. With automatic checks on, the console checks when it opens (the server reaches out at most once an hour); Check for updates asks again right away. Without internet access, upload the files instead.
updates.unavailable: Updates cannot be checked right now
updates.unavailableHelp: Make sure the server can reach the internet (set HTTPS_PROXY on its host if it needs a proxy). Without internet access, upload the system image catalog and the inference template catalog here, and upgrade the server with an uploaded release or gpuworks upgrade --archive.
updates.unpublished: Nothing has been published on the {{channel}} channel yet
updates.unpublishedHelp: The sources can be reached; this channel just has nothing on it yet. Switch to the other channel, or check again once a release is published. The system image catalog and the inference template catalog can still be updated here by uploading a file.
updates.invalidIndex: The sources answered with something that did not pass signature verification
updates.invalidIndexHelp: The server reached the sources but did not get a valid release index back, which usually means a gateway or proxy that requires signing in intercepted the request. Check the outbound proxy and gateway of the server's host and check again later; meanwhile, update by uploading files here.
updates.templatesApplied: Inference template catalog updated to {{version}} ({{count}} models)
updates.serverHelp: Where supported, upgrade the server here: it backs up first and rolls back when the new version does not come up. You can also run sudo gpuworks upgrade on its host; inside the office add --base-url for the internal release site, and an offline host uses --archive with a local release archive.
updates.serverConfirm: The server backs up its database, master key and current binary, then swaps the binary and restarts. The console and the /v1 gateway are unavailable for about a minute; inference on the nodes keeps running. If the new version does not come up, the backup and the current version are put back automatically.
updates.serverUpgrading: Upgrading from {{from}} to {{to}}; the server is restarting…
updates.serverUpgradingHelp: This page refreshes once the new version answers. If it does not come up, the server rolls back to the current version on its own.
updates.serverNotBack: {{version}} did not answer within 5 minutes and may have been rolled back; check the server log and install-history.jsonl in the install directory.
updates.superviseHost: On its host, run this to put it behind its supervisor; then it upgrades from here:
updates.superviseContainer: In a container, make this the container's start command:

blocker.no_service_manager: Nothing would start this process again after it exits (systemd, or gpuworks serve --supervise), so it cannot be upgraded from the console.
blocker.not_installed: The server was not installed with gpuworks install, so it cannot be upgraded from the console.
blocker.not_installed_binary: The server does not run the installed binary, so it cannot be upgraded from the console.
blocker.not_writable: The service account cannot write the install directory, so the server cannot be upgraded from the console.

updates.channelReleaseHelp: Only tagged releases: fewer updates, more stable.
updates.channelNightlyHelp: Every main-branch build: frequent updates, for early adopters and internal testing.
updates.autoCheckOnHelp: When on, opening the console checks the release sources for updates (the server asks at most once an hour), sending the server and agent version numbers.
updates.autoCheckOffHelp: Off: the server does not check by itself. "Check for updates" still reads the version index when you ask.
updates.notCheckedHelp: Automatic checks are off. Use "Check for updates" at the top right, or upload files here.

usageReport.title: User experience improvement program
usageReport.hint: Uploads runtime error and version information and usage counts; never records users' inputs or outputs.
usageReport.readOnly: Set usage_report in server.yaml to change it.

page.title: Settings
page.description: Manage branding, updates, where images and models are pulled from, node and deployment policy, security and access, and integrations such as AI services

branding.title: Branding
branding.description: Customize the logo, product name, header title and sign-in page text. Fields left empty use the built-in defaults, shown in the viewer's language; custom text is shown exactly as written, without translation.
branding.adminOnly: Only administrators can change the branding.
branding.logoHelp: Shown at the left of the top bar and on the sign-in page, scaled with its proportions to at most 160 px wide and 24 px high; wide or square images both work. PNG, JPEG, WebP, or SVG. You can crop it after uploading; raster images are scaled down to 256 px and compressed, and a small uncropped SVG is kept as is.
branding.productNameHelp: Shown in the browser tab title; once set, also shown under the logo on the sign-in page.
branding.consoleTitleHelp: Shown to the right of the logo in the top bar. Leave it empty to show the logo alone.
branding.loginDescriptionHelp: Shown on the left of the sign-in page; line breaks are kept.

crop.title: Crop logo
crop.help: Drag the selection to move it, drag a corner or edge to resize it, or drag outside it to draw a new one; arrow keys nudge it.

logoError.unreadable: This image cannot be read; try another one
logoError.tooLarge: The image is still larger than {{max}} KiB after compression; choose a simpler image

pull.title: Pull settings
pull.description: Where nodes get images and models from, and which proxy they go out through. Source rules say which alternative addresses to try first for image registries and model sites, proxies give the matching nodes their outbound proxy, sync groups (shared by images and models) say which nodes copy from one another, and credentials log in to private registries and give model sites a token. A deployment carries no source of its own; every node reads these settings when it pulls.

selector.semantics: Several values of one label match any of them; different labels must all match. To pick particular nodes, give them a label on the Nodes page first.
selector.placeholder: Pick or type key=value labels; leave empty for all nodes
selector.allNodes: No conditions: applies to all {{count}} nodes.
selector.noMatch: No node matches these labels right now. The setting is saved anyway and applies once a node carries them.
selector.countUnknown: The number of matching nodes is unavailable right now.

rules.intro: When the platform pulls an image or a model it tries the alternative addresses of the rules that match first, works down the list until one works, and finally goes back to the original address unless a rule turns that off. An image download moves on after a failure or 3 minutes without new bytes. For a model, an address that errors is skipped at once (and cooled for 30 minutes on that node); a connection that receives no data for 5 minutes counts as a stall, and two stalls in a row at the same address move on to the next. Image rules match registries; model site rules match an http(s) site root. Without a rule, the node probes each registry and orders them by reachability and latency.
rules.orderHint: Rules are matched from top to bottom.
rules.empty: No source rules. Nodes pull from each image's own registries, ordered by probing.
rules.deleteConfirmBody: Images it covered are then pulled by the remaining rules, or by probing the registries.
rules.matchHelp: The rule applies when an image reference starts with this registry host or prefix.
rules.matchPlaceholder: Registry host or prefix, such as docker.io, ghcr.io or gpuworks/
rules.endpointsHelp: Nodes try these in order before the original address.
rules.allowUpstreamHelp: After every alternative address fails, go back to the original address.
rules.noUpstreamWarning: Nodes only try the alternative addresses. If all of them fail, the pull fails.
rules.nodesHelp: Filter nodes by label. Empty means all nodes.
rules.typeHelp: Image rules match image registries; model site rules match model download sites. The type cannot change after saving.
rules.matchHelpUrl: The rule applies when a download address starts with this site root.
rules.endpointsHelpUrl: Nodes try these sites in order, then the original site.
rules.controlPlane: Used by the management node for model metadata
rules.controlPlaneHelp: The management node also finds addresses through this rule when it registers models, reads metadata and logos, and admits deployments.
rules.managementTestScope: This connectivity test runs from the selected compute nodes. It does not check outbound permission on the management node.

test.title: Test connectivity
test.help: The chosen nodes reach the addresses above the way a real download would (node proxy, no_proxy, credentials). The rule is not saved.
test.repoHelp: A small public repository is used; to prepare a gated model, enter its repository name.
test.authHelp: The site answered {{code}}: configure a token for this site under Credentials; the address itself is reachable.

rules.docsHint: Examples of common network setups: see the "Common network setups" section of docs/how-to/configure-pull-settings.md

groups.intro: Nodes only copy images and models automatically from nodes in the same sync group. When a direct connection fails, the node falls back to pulling from the registry within about 10 seconds. A node in no group never copies automatically.
groups.rules: A node in several groups may copy from any node of those groups, and the strictest rate limit of the groups two nodes share applies. To keep sites apart, delete the default-all-nodes group, which selects every node, and create one group per site.
groups.empty: No sync groups. No node copies images or models from another node automatically.
groups.name: Name
groups.selectorHelp: Nodes that carry these labels belong to the group. Empty means all nodes.
groups.rateHelp: Off means unlimited. The limit applies to the receiving node.
groups.rateRequired: Enter a rate greater than zero or turn the limit off.
groups.deleteConfirmBody: Nodes that are only in this group stop copying from other nodes automatically and pull from registries instead; nodes that are also in other groups keep copying within those. To have every node copy from every other again, create a group with no node conditions.

credentials.intro: One credential per host: a login for an image registry (user name and password) or a token for a model site. It is handed to a node only while it pulls and removed afterwards; the platform does not run docker login or change the node's own Docker configuration. Passwords and tokens are never shown again after saving.
credentials.typeRegistryHelp: Log in to a private image registry with a user name and a password or access token.
credentials.typeSiteHelp: Sent as a Bearer token only when the site is reached over https; mirrors and other sites never receive it. Hugging Face is the site confirmed to work so far.
credentials.hostHelp: The host name, with a port if it has one. A host can have only one credential.
credentials.usernameRequired: A registry login needs a user name.
credentials.secretHelp: A password or access token. It is stored encrypted and shown as dots after saving.
credentials.secretKeepHelp: Leave empty to keep the stored password.
credentials.tokenHelp: The site's access token. It is stored encrypted and shown as dots after saving.
credentials.tokenKeepHelp: Leave empty to keep the stored token.
credentials.deleteConfirmBody: Access to this host is then anonymous.

proxies.intro: Gives nodes their outbound proxy. A node uses the first proxy whose node requirements it meets, and at most one; with no match the node's agent uses its own environment. Addresses must not carry a login: the user name and password are separate fields, and the password is stored encrypted.
proxies.orderHint: Proxies are matched from top to bottom; the first match is used.
proxies.empty: No proxies yet; node agents use their own environment.
proxies.controlPlane: Used for management node outbound access
proxies.deleteConfirmBody: Nodes it covered then match the remaining proxies, or use the agent's own environment when none match.
proxies.httpProxyHelp: For http:// addresses, such as http://proxy.corp.example:3128, without a user name or password.
proxies.httpsProxyHelp: For https:// addresses; fill in at least one of this and the HTTP proxy.
proxies.noProxyHelp: Same syntax as the NO_PROXY environment variable, such as localhost,10.0.0.0/8,.corp; the platform also adds loopback and the management node address
proxies.passwordKeepHelp: A password is stored; leave empty to keep it.
proxies.passwordClearedHelp: The stored password is removed on save.
proxies.controlPlaneLabel: Used for management node outbound access
proxies.controlPlaneHelp: The management node goes out through this proxy to read model metadata and logos, register catalog URLs, probe image archive URLs and test credential logins.
proxies.nodesHelp: Filter by node labels; leave empty for every node.
proxies.previewTitle: Preview the proxy a node uses
proxies.previewNone: This node uses no proxy; its agent uses its own environment.

sshKey.title: SSH Key
sshKey.description: The server's own SSH key pair. Adding nodes, prechecks and out-of-band recovery sign in with it, so a node only has to authorize the public key below once. The private key is stored encrypted and never shown.
sshKey.importHelp: Use a key your nodes already trust as the platform key. Only unencrypted OpenSSH or PKCS#8 private keys are accepted; it replaces the current key.
sshKey.rotateWarning: Nodes that only authorized the current public key will stop accepting the server, and their out-of-band recovery fails until they authorize the new one.
sshKey.loadFailed: Could not load the platform SSH key: {{detail } }

deployment.title: Deployment
deployment.description: Defaults for every deployment in the cluster; a deployment can set its own in the deploy form's Runtime section.
deployment.startTimeoutHelp: How long a started instance may take to pass the engine health check before the start counts as failed and is retried. Deployments that set no timeout of their own use this value; a change applies to instances started afterwards. Range {{min}}–{{max}} s.

terminal.title: Web Terminal
terminal.description: The Web Terminal opens a compute node's host shell directly in the browser and is available only to administrators. Auditing records metadata only (operator, node, duration, and transferred bytes).
terminal.privacy: No terminal input or output content is recorded.
terminal.enabledHelp: When disabled, terminal entry points on all nodes stop working immediately and existing sessions are denied reconnection.
terminal.idleHelp: Only operator input counts as activity; continuously producing commands such as watch nvidia-smi do not renew the timeout.
terminal.graceHelp: Closing a session sends SIGTERM first. If the process does not exit within this period, the entire session receives SIGKILL to prevent leftover processes from occupying VRAM.
terminal.nodeLimitHelp: New terminal requests return 429 after this limit is reached.
terminal.globalLimitHelp: Must not be lower than the per-node limit.

orphanCleanup.title: Orphan Container Cleanup
orphanCleanup.description: When enabled, each agent removes gpuworks-named containers that are absent from its desired state on every state sync.

security.title: Security
security.description: Platform-wide switches that trade convenience for exposure. Change them only if you understand who can reach what.
security.previewNetwork: Allow playground HTML previews to make network requests
security.previewNetworkHelp: Off: a preview may load scripts, styles and images from HTTPS sites, but its fetch, XHR and WebSocket calls and any plain-HTTP resources are blocked. On: no network restrictions apply, so a page generated by a model can reach any address the viewer's browser can, including intranet services and this console's own address. The preview never gets the console's login session either way.
security.inferenceOpenAccess: Accept /v1 inference requests without a token
security.inferenceOpenAccessHelp: Off: every /v1 request must present an inference token; a request without one is refused. On: a request that presents no token is served anonymously, so anyone who can reach this server can call the deployed models and consume their GPUs. A request that does present a token is still verified. Revoking the last token no longer opens the gateway; only this switch does.
security.adminOnly: Only administrators can change security settings.

telemetry.title: Request trace export (OpenTelemetry)
telemetry.description: Send every gateway request as an OTLP span to your OpenTelemetry Collector, which forwards it to Jaeger, Tempo, Grafana Cloud, Datadog or another tracing backend. When the upstream gateway sends a traceparent, the platform's span joins its trace. Spans carry the model, tokens, cache hits, the time of each phase (queue, prefill, reasoning, answer) and the result. Prompts and replies are never exported.
telemetry.adminOnly: Only administrators can change the export settings.
telemetry.settingError: The saved export settings cannot be applied, so export is stopped. Save the settings again to recover.
telemetry.endpointHelp: The OTLP/HTTP address, for example http://otel-collector:4318; /v1/traces is added when the path is not already that. The server must reach it; nodes need not.
telemetry.headersHelp: Sent with every export, for example an authorization token or a tenant id. Values are stored encrypted and not shown again; leave a saved one empty to keep it.
telemetry.sampleRatioHelp: Applies to the traces the gateway starts itself; a trace whose upstream already decided keeps that decision. The platform's own request view is not affected.
telemetry.traceLinkHelp: A tracing backend URL containing {trace_id}; with it, a trace id in the request details opens there. Optional.
telemetry.testHelp: Sends one span named gpuworks test span with what is filled in now (no need to save first).
telemetry.testOK: The collector accepted the test span
telemetry.testTrace: Search the tracing backend for this trace id:

mcp.title: MCP service
mcp.description: Lets AI tools such as Claude Code and Cursor read this platform over MCP: the cluster overview, API search and reads, the metric catalog and GPU topology. The tools are the AI assistant's own: read-only, reading with the token owner's permissions, with credentials redacted the same way.
mcp.adminOnly: Only an administrator can turn it on or off.
mcp.authText: Send a platform API token (read is enough): Authorization: Bearer gwp_…
mcp.dataNotice: An MCP client hands what it reads to the model it is configured with; where the data goes is the client's choice, not the platform's AI service setting.

listen.title: Listen addresses
listen.description: The addresses this server binds on this host (plus 127.0.0.1 for local tools), stored in server.yaml. They only decide where this server answers; nodes, users and API clients choose the address they use to reach it, and a domain, reverse proxy or NAT forwarding to these works as well.
listen.consoleHelp: IP:port the Web console and management API bind on this host. Separate several with commas. Node connections and the inference API use it too unless set under Advanced.
listen.agentHelp: IP:port this server binds on this host for agents to connect and download the installer. The address an agent dials is the --server in its install command (entered when adding a node, the browser's address by default); a domain, reverse proxy or NAT address works as long as it forwards here. Installed agents keep dialing their original address after a change: if it no longer forwards to the new listen address they go offline until the forwarding is adjusted or they are reinstalled.
listen.gatewayHelp: IP:port the OpenAI-compatible /v1 API binds on this host, for example on a business network. Clients may reach it through a reverse proxy or NAT.
listen.saved: Saved. The new addresses take effect after a restart.
listen.pending: Saved addresses differ from what the server is bound to; they take effect after a restart.
listen.restartCommand: Nothing restarts this server automatically. Run on its host: {{command}}
listen.overridden: The server was started with --addr, which overrides server.yaml; remove it to manage addresses here.
listen.noConfig: The server was started without server.yaml, so its addresses cannot be changed here.

ai.notice: The platform is fully usable without AI configuration. Configure a service to enable deployment advice, error diagnosis, and model Q&A.
ai.egressNotice: The assistant reads the platform data the asking user can see - nodes, deployments, models, logs and metrics - and sends what it reads to the AI service in use ({{host}}). To keep it inside the platform, use a model served by this platform.
ai.name: Name
ai.deleteConfirm: Delete “{{name}}”? The assistant stops using it in this configuration.
ai.deletedPromoted: Configuration deleted. The assistant now uses “{{name}}”.
ai.defaultLocked: This is the service the assistant uses. Mark another service as the default to move it.
ai.baseUrlHint: Fill the address up to /v1. Do not include /chat/completions: the platform appends it.
ai.keyKeep: Leave blank to keep the stored key
ai.testConnection: Cannot reach the address: check the host, the port and the network
ai.testBlocked: The platform's outbound policy refuses this address; an administrator must allow the host
ai.testAuth: The API key was rejected: check the upstream key
ai.testPath: The address answered 404 but named no model, so the path is wrong. Fill it up to /v1, without /chat/completions
ai.testModel: The service does not serve this model: check the model name
ai.testHttp: The service answered with an unexpected status

dataRetention.title: Data retention
dataRetention.description: How long each kind of data is kept, how much space it may take, and the time zone daily statistics are counted in. Saving applies at once; what a shorter retention no longer keeps is deleted in the background.
dataRetention.configNote: metrics_retention in the configuration file only sets the first start's retention of metrics and logs; from then on this setting decides.
dataRetention.billing: Billing record, set on its own
dataRetention.shrinkBody: After shortening these, what they no longer keep is deleted in the background and cannot be recovered: {{fields}}.
dataRetention.passFailed: A background cleanup or roll-up failed
dataRetention.requestsNote: Whichever limit is reached first applies; under heavy traffic the size limit usually comes first. Today's data is never deleted.

switches.quality: Service quality: request outcomes, first-token and end-to-end latency
switches.gpu: GPU utilization: utilization, memory, power, temperature
switches.gpu_time: GPU hours: cards each deployment held × hours

alwaysOn.scheduling: Scheduling activity: scheduling events by reason, card switches, sharing deployments' awake time (always counted)

metrics.title: Raw metric samples
metrics.description: Raw samples of nodes, GPUs, engines and the gateway; the monitoring charts read them.

logs.title: Container logs
logs.description: Output of inference engines and containers; log search reads it.

requests.title: Request records
requests.description: The gateway's record of every request (timing, tokens, outcome); the monitoring request view reads it.

usage.title: Token usage
usage.description: Tokens every API key used on every deployment, by hour and by day, never sampled; usage analytics and billing read it.

stats.title: Service quality / GPU utilization / GPU hours / scheduling activity
stats.description: The long-term statistics of usage analytics and scheduling analysis share one retention; the first three can be switched off one by one, and a statistic switched off stops counting and what it has ages out.

zone.title: Statistics time zone
zone.description: Where days start for daily statistics. A change applies to days rolled up after it; days already rolled up stay.

experience.title: Feature experience mode
experience.portHint: Uses port {{port}}; open it in the firewall to reach it from other computers. Each time it is turned on, the initial data is restored and a new password is generated.
experience.resetConfirm: Discard what was done in the experience environment and restore the initial data?
experience.passwordConfirm: Generate a new password? Signed-in sessions in the experience environment end and must sign in again with the new password.

diagnostics.adminOnly: Only administrators can start debug collection and collect diagnostics.

bundle.title: Collect diagnostics
bundle.description: Packs the server log for a time range, the related nodes' agent logs and diagnosis reports, instance logs, debug collection records, and the related nodes, deployments, events, images, storages, settings and request records into one archive to download and send to support. Credentials keep only their first 8 characters; prompts and replies are not included (except in requests a debug collection recorded). Archives are kept for {{days}} days.
bundle.rangeRequired: Choose a start and end time.
bundle.doctorHelp: Runs a diagnosis on each collected node (up to about 2 minutes) and includes the result.
bundle.deploymentsHelp: Collects these deployments' configuration, events, request records and instance logs; with no node chosen, the agent logs of the nodes they run on.
bundle.nodesHelp: Collects these nodes' agent logs; at most {{max}}.
bundle.started: Collecting; download it below when it is ready.
bundle.truncated: Reached its size limit; only part was kept

itemReason.unsupported: The node's agent version does not support it

debug.title: Debug collection
debug.description: For a while, writes the server's and the chosen nodes' agent debug logs to separate files, and records each request of the chosen deployments in full (the request, every frame the engine returned and every frame the client received, and how it ended). Regular log levels are unchanged; it ends by itself when the time is up or the size is reached. Collecting diagnostics picks up debug collections that overlap its time range.

nodeReason.unsupported: The node's agent version does not support it

debug.contentWarning: The chosen deployments' requests are recorded in full, prompts and replies included. Records stay on the server and the nodes only, and are deleted after {{days}} days.
debug.sizeHelp: Server log and request records together, at most {{max}} GiB; each node's agent log is limited to {{node}}, and one request records at most {{request}}.
debug.deploymentsHelp: Records these deployments' requests in full and turns on agent debug logs on the nodes they run on.
debug.nodesHelp: Turns on agent debug logs on these nodes.
debug.startConfirm: Start debug collection? The chosen deployments' request contents will be recorded.
